claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that the body of work he will be most proud of at death is his books, not the businesses he has built — placing written knowledge contribution above business creation as his highest-order personal metric.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Alex Hormozi states that great writing comes from a place of wanting to add to the body of knowledge — framing genuine contribution as the motivational source that separates high-quality written content from promotional or entertainment content.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: written long-form content (books, not short-form or video)
claims.mechanism: Authentic intent to contribute knowledge produces substantively different output than intent to entertain or sell, because the author's filter for what to include changes.
bounded_by: Does not address whether entertainment-first intent can still produce knowledge value

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's book $100 Million Offers sold over 430,000 copies and was launched before he had a built audience — demonstrating that a sufficiently strong written offer can generate substantial organic distribution without a pre-existing platform.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: book-format product (not a course or coaching offer)
launched circa 2021 on Amazon without prior large social audience

numbers.axis: copies sold for $100 Million Offers by Alex Hormozi

bounded_by: Single data point; does not prove all books launched without audience achieve similar distribution

practices.text: Invite your personal network to live launch events for maximum attendance and energy.
